title: G6 sensor restart problems with xDrip
symptom: After restarting a Dexcom G6 sensor after 10 days, the user initially saw a warm-up period but then got a 'sensor failed start' message. A notification 'Auto Start Sensor Requesting Restart' appears but clicking it does nothing. Restarting the collector and re-pairing the transmitter did not help.
cause: The thread does not explicitly identify a root cause, but opasha suggests that the sensor's gold dot area and the transmitter's black rubber tips may be dirty, causing connection issues. Also, the 0000 method is said to do nothing.
fix: The proven method described by opasha: Stop sensor, remove transmitter for at least 15 minutes, clean the sensor's gold dots and the transmitter's black rubber tips, reconnect, start sensor as new with the same code (not 0000), wait 2 hours and a few minutes for warm-up. This method was confirmed to work by mrazek.
evidence_quote: This is the proven way to make it work: 1) Stop Sensor 2) Remove the transmitter with thin plastic (guitar pick or glucometer test strip) - set a time for 15 minutes - no less 3) Wipe down the sensor's two gold dot area - this gets sweat/oil/soap/water on it, so it needs to be completely cleaned to be functional - anything in the way will cause errors - MAKE SURE TO KEEP THE TRANSMITTER NEAR YOUR PHONE DURING THIS TIME. 4) Carefully clean the black rubber tips on your sensor on your arm - this is the point of contact those gold circle sensors make from your transmitter. Yes, they both need to be clean before contact with each other - I have tested this many times - the cleaner the contact, the longer your sensor can last - I have done 2 re-start sessions and got up to 27 days once. 5) After the 15 minutes are up and sensor and transmitter are cleaned, reconnect them and make sure your phone is still connected to your transmitter 6) Start Sensor as if brand new - enter the present time and date when asked and enter the same code for your transmitter - do not do the 0000 method - it does nothing 7) Wait 2 hours and a few minutes (for the final warm up) and it will automatically resume
